# Region Nordjylland — Nordjylland

Region Nordjylland and the broader geographic area of Nordjylland represent one of Denmark's five administrative regions, playing a critical role in the national psychiatric healthcare system. In the context of the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]], Region Nordjylland serves as both an organizational entity reporting clinical data and a geographic region whose patient outcomes are tracked across multiple quality indicators. The dual identity of Region Nordjylland (the administrative organization) and Nordjylland (the geographic region) is central to understanding regional disparities in ADHD assessment and treatment across Denmark.

In recent reporting periods, Region Nordjylland has exhibited significant fluctuations and distinct performance metrics across various indicators. For instance, the region experienced a 16% increase in the number of assessment processes, serving as a comparative baseline for other regions [^src1]. When evaluating early childhood assessments, Nordjylland recorded a 64% fulfillment rate for [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] [^src15], and a 30% fulfillment rate for Indicator 2a [^src2]. For older children, the region achieved a 31% fulfillment rate for [[indicator-2b|indicator-2b]] [^src3]. Notably, Region Nordjylland reported the highest regional performance for [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] at 34%, contrasting sharply with the 10% seen in [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] [^src4].

However, the region also faces substantial operational and capacity challenges. Due to capacity constraints in child and youth psychiatry, Region Nordjylland referred approximately 50 children and adolescents per month to private providers for assessment during the reporting period, which significantly impacted the data for the first three assessment indicators [^src7]. Furthermore, there are notable registration challenges; internal analyses reveal that while many children and young people receive the relevant procedures, they often do so after the mandated 90- or 120-day time limits, affecting target fulfillment [^src14]. For the adult population, low fulfillment rates are primarily attributed to registration errors, prompting general psychiatric departments to implement corrective measures to ensure data accurately reflects clinical practice [^src14].

Performance across other indicators highlights a mixed landscape. Region Nordjylland scored 33% on [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src10] but recorded the highest medication rate among all regions at 82% for [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] [^src10]. Conversely, the region reported the lowest result for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] at 18%, compared to 50% in [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] [^src11]. In terms of educational outcomes for young people in the [[adhd-udredningspopulation|ADHD-udredningspopulation]] and [[adhd-behandlingspopulation|ADHD-behandlingspopulation]], Nordjylland recorded the lowest rates of passed exit exams at 47% and 49%, respectively, while [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] led with 63% and 69% [^src16]. For [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]], results were at 0% [^src17], and like all other regions, Nordjylland failed to meet the targets for [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] [^src12]. On a positive note, the region achieved the highest score for [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] at 85% [^src13]. Additionally, data shows that in the [[adhd-behandlingspopulation|behandlingspopulationen]], there were no registered patients in the 0–5 age group in Region Nordjylland [^src6], and there are significant regional variations in the usage of the process marker [[agx01b|AGX01B]] [^src7].

Together, these data points illustrate a region grappling with capacity limits and registration hurdles, yet achieving top marks in specific clinical metrics like medication rates and Indicator 11. The ongoing efforts to correct registration practices and manage patient overflow to private actors underscore the dynamic challenges faced by Region Nordjylland in delivering and documenting ADHD care.
